messages:
ravi: Heads up — ran a perfetto + nsys sweep on the latest kvcache-prefetch branch. Seeing weird H2D tail latencies and long peer-copy scatter entries, looks like pageable backpressure. timeline attached below, paste of hot segments.

alisa: can you paste the nsys slice? quick top-level numbers ok.

ravi: pasted snippet from nsys GPU timeline — timestamps are ms relative to trace start:
```
0.0  memcpy H2D  device0 <- host pageable  0.8ms
12.4 memcpy H2D  device0 <- host pageable  1.1ms
24.2 memcpy H2D  device0 <- host pageable  87.9ms  <-- huge stall
24.4 kernel  attn_forward  2.0ms
112.5 memcpy peer-to-peer  gpu1->gpu0 (nvlink) 0.9ms
113.4 memcpy H2D  device0 <- host pageable  45.2ms
```
Looks like occasional huge pageable H2D spikes that line up with our KV prefetch windows. Also saw lots of short scatter-gather host->multiple-gpu memcpy ops instead of a single pinned batch.

mike: are those cudaMemcpyAsync from worker threads? or cuMemcpy? pageable host memory will do sync staging and cause host fallthrough -> long H2D. If threads call blocking cudaMemcpy that will stall CPU and GPU. Any use of cudaHostRegister or pinned alloc?

ravi: we don't currently pin in the prefetch path — trying to avoid extra allocations per request. Prefetch currently does small chained memcpy calls for each cache line:
```
for segment in segments:
  cudaMemcpyAsync(dev + off, host + seg.off, seg.len, H2D, stream)
```
We batch by stream but not by coalescing segments.

sheila: that loop pattern can create a lot of scatter-gather descriptors and cause the driver to fallback to pageable transfer path (hostfallthrough) or serialize. Two immediate fixes to test:
- Use cudaHostAlloc/pinned buffers for the prefetch buffer pool and memcpy from pinned region.
- Coalesce segments into a single contiguous buffer (or use staged pinned slab) before issuing a single async transfer.

ravi: yeah thought about a slab. But worried about memory pressure. Also KV prefetch frequency is adaptive — sometimes dozens of tiny segments in parallel across requests. That seems to correlate with the big 87ms spike.

perf-bot: perf regression alert: RTT p50 on small requests increased 20% on kvcache-prefetch (canary). Top contributor: host -> device memcpy spikes. See trace id perf-2026-03-14-180250.

alisa: quick repro plan:
1) run nsys with stream markers around prefetch and the downstream kernel, capture API and memcpy stacks.
2) run with cudaHostRegister on existing buffers and compare histograms.
3) perfetto to check whether those H2D events are queued or blocked by CPU scheduling (hostthread preemption).

mike: also check if we are using cudaMemcpyAsync on pageable memory (it enqueues but uses driver staged copies — big latency). Using cudaHostRegister turns them into genuine async DMA.

ravi: I ran a short A/B earlier: pinned allocation reduced the large spikes; sample numbers:
- pageable: p95 memcpy H2D = 60ms, p99 = 120ms
- pinned: p95 memcpy H2D = 2.3ms, p99 = 6.1ms
So huge improvement but cost in RAM. Planning to implement a pooled pinned slab per GPU and attempt to copy into that slab from request threads, then single cuMemcpyAsync to device.

sheila: another angle — batching heuristics. If we wait 1-2ms to aggregate segments per request we can reduce scatter. But this increases tail latency for the first token. Maybe do dynamic delay: small requests (<2kb) wait 0.5ms to batch; large requests go through immediate path. Also consider prefix-aware kv prefetch: prefetch coalesced ranges instead of fine-grained keys when hot.

ravi: good notes. I'll prototype pinned-slab + coalesce + dynamic batching. Can someone help validate NVLink peer-copy ordering? There's a case where peer copies fire during H2D spikes and may compete on PCIe link causing contention.

mike: NVLink peer copies (gpu->gpu) should be mostly independent unless copies from host also traverse the same PCIe root complex to an intermediary. On our topology, gpu1->gpu0 over NVLink but host->gpu0 goes over PCIe root; contention can occur if driver serializes DMA engines. Need perfetto to show DMA engine timelines (eg AER/GTX queue). Use nsight systems with kernel metric for memcpy engines.

ravi: will run targeted perfetto with CRIU markers and collect DMA engine counters. Also add a test that pins the source and issues a single coalesced copy vs many small ones.

sheila: long term we should add a runtime knob: if pages_unpinned_stalls > threshold, auto-upgrade prefetch to use pinned slab for that tenant. Avoid global memory tax.

ravi: Agreed. Action items:
- ravi: prototype pinned-slab + single coalesced memcpy (ETA 48h)
- alisa: run nsight/perfetto config and capture DMA engine timelines (ETA 24h)
- mike: help with NVLink topology verification and driver flags to prefer P2P DMA (ETA 24h)
- sheila: spec dynamic batching heuristic and threshold heuristic for auto-pin (ETA 72h)

mike: FYI there was a kernel regression PR touching allocator code last week — might be related. I'll bisect if we still see spikes after pinned-slab.

ravi: thanks all — attaching perf links once traces are uploaded. :thumbsup:
